question: What two main elements make up the foundation of modern professional nursing?

options.A: Art and science
options.B: Administration and finance
options.C: Theory and politics
options.D: History and geography

explanation: Nursing combines the emotional and human connection of art with the empirical clinical knowledge of science to care for patients effectively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is relying only on medical facts without empathy not enough for a nurse?

options.A: It automatically leads to immediate legal prosecution
options.B: It prevents the nurse from writing doctors' prescriptions
options.C: It misses the human touch needed for true healing
options.D: It violates standard hospital financial guidelines

explanation: You've got this! Clinical facts alone cannot address the emotional and spiritual suffering of a sick human being. Great nursing always requires genuine compassion. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: Who is widely recognized as the pioneer of modern professional nursing?

options.A: Mary Seacole
options.B: Linda Richards
options.C: Clara Barton
options.D: Florence Nightingale

explanation: Florence Nightingale transformed nursing during the Crimean War by emphasizing sanitation, organization, and formal training. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: How has the primary role of the nurse changed from early historical times to today?

options.A: It evolved from informal domestic charity to an autonomous regulated profession
options.B: It changed from independent medical diagnosis to unpaid domestic work
options.C: It shifted from hospital administration to strictly religious duties
options.D: It transformed from a male-only military role to a purely clerical office job

explanation: Think about how far we've come! Modern nursing requires formal education, licensing, and independent critical thinking, rather than just basic home caregiving. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which global body defines nursing as autonomous and collaborative care for people of all ages in all settings?

options.A: West African Health Organization
options.B: International Council of Nurses
options.C: Red Cross International
options.D: World Medical Association

explanation: Spot on! The International Council of Nurses sets the global standard definition that highlights both our independent and teamwork roles in healthcare. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of these activities is a core part of the global definition of nursing?

options.A: Filing hospital tax returns and insurance claims
options.B: Promoting healthy lifestyles in local communities
options.C: Purchasing pharmaceutical drugs for wholesale markets
options.D: Designing architectural layouts for new surgical suites

explanation: Nursing goes beyond treating sick people in wards; we also actively promote health and prevent illness right inside our communities! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four central concepts in the nursing metaparadigm?

options.A: Medication
options.B: Health
options.C: Environment
options.D: Person

explanation: Easy to remember: the four pillars are Person, Environment, Health, and Nursing. Medication is just a tool we use, not a core pillar! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: How do nursing theorists define 'health' within our professional framework?

options.A: A dynamic state of physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: The complete elimination of all hospital admissions nationwide
options.C: The total absence of any identifiable bacteria in the blood
options.D: A static condition achieved strictly through pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health isn't just the literal absence of sickness. In nursing, we see it as a flowing, everyday state of overall physical, mental, and social well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: When a nurse steps up to protect a patient's rights and safety, what role are they playing?

options.A: Advocate
options.B: Surgical operator
options.C: Pharmacist
options.D: Hospital accountant

explanation: You got it! Being an advocate means standing up for your patients' rights, safety, and best interests when they are most vulnerable. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: A nurse takes time to explain a new diabetic diet to a confused patient and their family. What role is this nurse performing?

options.A: Radiologist
options.B: Laboratory technician
options.C: Facility director
options.D: Educator

explanation: Teaching patients and families how to manage their health and care for themselves at home is a core part of our educator role. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: What does professional accountability primarily require a nurse to do?

options.A: Avoid asking senior doctors for professional guidance
options.B: Cover up small mistakes to prevent hospital lawsuits
options.C: Take responsibility for their clinical actions and decisions
options.D: Work twenty-four-hour shifts without taking a break

explanation: Accountability simply means owning your choices and accepting the professional results of the care you give. We stand tall by our actions! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is following a strict code of ethics so important for a nurse?

options.A: It ensures the nurse receives the highest possible salary tier
options.B: It eliminates the need for any formal continuing education classes
options.C: It guarantees patient confidentiality, dignity, and fairness in care
options.D: It grants the nurse legal authority to perform major surgeries

explanation: Our ethical code is our compass. It guides us to treat every patient fairly, keep their secrets safe, and always respect their human dignity. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which statutory body is responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: Nigerian Medical and Dental Council
options.B: Federal Ministry of Internal Affairs
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: West African Medical Association

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the sole legal regulatory authority for the nursing profession in the country. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of regulatory bodies like the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: To manage the commercial business accounts of private hospitals
options.B: To protect the public by ensuring safe and competent nursing practice
options.C: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.D: To decide which political party wins national health elections

explanation: Spot on! Professional councils exist primarily to keep the public safe by setting high educational and ethical standards for all practicing nurses. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: Who primarily handled the care of sick family members in most ancient households?

options.A: Professional monastic orders
options.B: Government-certified physicians
options.C: Women within the home
options.D: Trained military nurses

explanation: Before formal institutions, caring for the sick was mainly a domestic duty performed by female family members. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: How did ancient Greek medicine under Hippocrates differ from earlier mystical approaches?

options.A: It prohibited the use of herbal remedies and plant extracts
options.B: It relied entirely on spiritual sacrifices and ritual prayers
options.C: It viewed disease as a natural process rather than divine punishment
options.D: It used modern laboratory testing and surgical antibiotics

explanation: Hippocrates and his followers shifted the focus toward rational observation of symptoms and natural causes of illness. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: What type of institution served as the primary sanctuary for healing during the early medieval period?

options.A: Monasteries and convents
options.B: Private community pharmacies
options.C: University teaching clinics
options.D: Government public health offices

explanation: Religious institutions like monasteries and convents housed the earliest organized healthcare and nursing services. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why did military nursing groups become so important during the Crusades?

options.A: To translate ancient Greek philosophy texts
options.B: To provide organized shelter and treat wounded soldiers
options.C: To manufacture advanced gunpowder and tactical weapons
options.D: To govern newly conquered political territories

explanation: During the Crusades, special nursing groups were needed to set up safe resting places and care for fighters and travelers who got hurt.

question: What was the primary focus of Florence Nightingale's interventions during the Crimean War?

options.A: Hospital financial management
options.B: Pharmaceutical drug development
options.C: Advanced surgical operations
options.D: Environmental sanitation and hygiene

explanation: Nightingale drastically reduced mortality by improving ventilation, cleanliness, hand hygiene, and nutrition. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h3)

question: A nurse implements strict handwashing and ensures a clean, well-ventilated ward to prevent infection outbreaks. Whose historical principles are being applied here?

options.A: Hippocrates
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Ransome-Kuti
options.D: Mary Seacole

explanation: Focusing on environmental factors and hygiene to promote healing is the core hallmark of Nightingale's nursing philosophy. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h3)

question: Who played the primary role in introducing Western-style nursing and hospitals to Nigeria during the colonial era?

options.A: Missionary societies
options.B: Military combat units
options.C: International trade unions
options.D: Local traditional rulers

explanation: Christian missions established the earliest Western hospitals and introduced formal nursing concepts to Nigeria. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: How did nursing education in Nigeria change after the country gained independence in 1960?

options.A: Universities began offering degree programs in nursing science
options.B: Training was moved entirely out of hospitals into military camps
options.C: All foreign-trained nurses were banned from practicing locally
options.D: Traditional herbalism completely replaced western pharmacology

explanation: After independence, nursing grew rapidly as a profession, and Nigerian universities started offering degree courses to elevate nurse training.

question: What is the main job of nursing regulatory bodies like the Nursing and Midwifery Council?

options.A: To protect the public by enforcing standards and scopes of practice
options.B: To construct new hospital buildings across the country
options.C: To negotiate hospital employee salaries and retirement pensions
options.D: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs and medical equipment

explanation: Regulatory bodies like NMCN exist to protect patients by making sure all practicing nurses are well-trained, ethical, and competent.

question: Why did nursing training move away from simple hospital-based apprenticeships toward university degrees?

options.A: To reduce the total number of practicing nurses in the workforce
options.B: To eliminate the need for clinical bedside practice entirely
options.C: To build an evidence-based foundation and professional autonomy
options.D: To ensure students spent more time doing manual hospital chores

explanation: Moving nursing into universities gives students the strong scientific reasoning and independent thinking skills needed in modern healthcare.

question: Which tool has become a standard digital replacement for paper patient charts in modern healthcare facilities?

options.A: Printed pocket notebooks
options.B: Electronic health records
options.C: Manual bedside blackboards
options.D: Audio cassette recordings

explanation: Electronic health records allow fast, secure sharing of patient data across interprofessional healthcare teams. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge currently facing the nursing profession worldwide?

options.A: Managing chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: Complete elimination of all patient illnesses
options.C: Shortages of qualified nursing personnel
options.D: High rates of workplace stress and burnout

explanation: We haven't wiped out all illnesses yet! Instead, nurses worldwide battle daily with staff shortages, burnout, and rising chronic illnesses.

question: How does the World Health Organization (WHO) officially define health?

options.A: The total absence of any infection or physical pain
options.B: The ability to work and function normally in society
options.C: A balance between spiritual and biological body forces
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being

explanation: You've got this! The WHO looks at the whole person. Health isn't just about a strong body; it includes how we feel mentally and how we relate to others around us.

question: What is the main difference between an 'illness' and a 'disease'?

options.A: Disease can be cured by nursing care, but illness requires surgery.
options.B: Illness is a subjective feeling of being unwell, while disease is a physical alteration in body function.
options.C: Illness is diagnosed by laboratory tests, while disease is felt by the patient.
options.D: Illness only affects mental stability, whereas disease strictly affects organs.

explanation: Think of it this way: disease is the actual physical problem happening inside the body, while illness is how the patient actually experiences and feels that problem.

question: What are the two opposite ends of the Illness-Wellness Continuum?

options.A: Physical weakness and mental strength
options.B: Acute infection and chronic disability
options.C: Hospital admission and complete recovery
options.D: Premature death and high-level wellness

explanation: The continuum ranges from death on the left to optimal wellness on the right. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h2)

question: A patient takes daily medication that successfully controls their high blood pressure. However, they feel drained, skip workouts, and eat junk food. Where do they fit on the wellness scale?

options.A: Completely outside the continuum because they take medication
options.B: At the far left end experiencing premature death
options.C: In the neutral point, free of disease symptoms but below optimal wellness
options.D: At the far right end representing high-level wellness

explanation: Spot on! Keeping symptoms under control puts them in the safe middle zone. True wellness takes a bit more active care with lifestyle habits.

question: Which health model looks at wellness strictly as having no physical signs or symptoms of sickness?

options.A: Role performance model
options.B: Clinical model
options.C: Adaptive model
options.D: Eudaimonistic model

explanation: You've got this! The clinical model is the classic medical approach: if nothing hurts and you have no visible sickness, you are healthy.

question: A patient says, 'I cannot be healthy because I am too weak to go to work and look after my children.' Which health model are they using?

options.A: Clinical model
options.B: Role performance model
options.C: Eudaimonistic model
options.D: Biological germ model

explanation: Spot on! This model measures health by whether a person can successfully carry out their daily family and job responsibilities.

question: Which dimension of health involves the ability to handle daily stress and express feelings properly?

options.A: Spiritual dimension
options.B: Emotional dimension
options.C: Intellectual dimension
options.D: Environmental dimension

explanation: The emotional dimension focuses on mental resilience, coping mechanisms, and emotional expression. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h4)

question: After losing their job, a person faces eviction, can no longer afford good food, and falls into deep depression. Which health areas are affected here?

options.A: Only the role performance dimension
options.B: Environmental, economic, emotional, and physical
options.C: Only the physical and intellectual dimensions
options.D: Strictly the spiritual and clinical dimensions

explanation: Fantastic! Life events don't happen in a vacuum. Losing a job touches housing (environmental), food (physical), money (economic), and mood (emotional) all at once.

question: What is the very first thing that happens when a person starts developing an illness?

options.A: Seeking medical care
options.B: Experiencing symptoms
options.C: Entering rehabilitation
options.D: Assuming the sick role

explanation: Easy and logical! The illness journey always starts when the person physically or mentally notices that something feels off in their body.

question: A patient stays home from work, complains of body aches to their partner, and rests in bed. Which stage of illness behavior is this?

options.A: Dependent client role
options.B: Assuming the sick role
options.C: Recovery stage
options.D: Medical care contact stage

explanation: Spot on! At this stage, the person accepts that they are sick, gets support from loved ones, and takes a break from their normal daily duties.

question: Which of these is an example of an internal factor that can affect a person's health?

options.A: Cultural family traditions
options.B: Availability of community hospitals
options.C: Genetic makeup and inherited traits
options.D: Socioeconomic income level

explanation: You've got this! Internal factors come from within us—like our genes, age, and sex—while external factors come from our surroundings.

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand a patient's cultural background regarding health?

options.A: Culture completely prevents patients from experiencing chronic pain.
options.B: Culture shapes how clients interpret symptoms and choose where to seek care.
options.C: Culture determines the exact medical dosage a patient's liver can metabolize.
options.D: Culture is the single biological cause of all infectious diseases.

explanation: Great thinking! Culture heavily influences whether someone trusts modern medicine, traditional healing, or a mix of both when they feel sick.

question: What is a common emotional reaction when an adult suddenly comes down with an acute illness?

options.A: Complete indifference to hospital rules
options.B: Enhanced self-confidence at work
options.C: Immediate increase in physical strength
options.D: Loss of independence and anxiety

explanation: Naturally! Having to rely on others for basic care can make adult patients feel vulnerable, worried, and anxious.

question: When a mother of young children is admitted to the hospital for major surgery, what is the most likely effect on her family?

options.A: Family members will immediately stop working to stay in the hospital room.
options.B: Household expenses will decrease due to reduced grocery shopping.
options.C: The family structure remains entirely unchanged during hospital stays.
options.D: Family roles must be rearranged to cover childcare and household duties.

explanation: Spot on! When a key caregiver falls ill, family routines get disrupted, forcing other members to step up and handle chores and childcare.

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care when using the concept of basic human needs?

options.A: Discharging the patient as quickly as possible
options.B: Focusing on the whole person and their essential requirements
options.C: Treating only the diagnosed disease process
options.D: Managing hospital administrative tasks

explanation: Looking at basic human needs helps nurses care for the entire individual rather than just treating a specific illness. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why does a hospital admission often disrupt a patient's ability to meet basic human needs?

options.A: Hospital environments completely eliminate stress
options.B: Patients no longer care about their personal health
options.C: Familiar daily routines and independence are interrupted
options.D: Healthcare providers automatically handle all needs instantly

explanation: Being in an unfamiliar hospital setting takes away a person's normal independence, making basic tasks harder to manage alone. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: According to Maslow's hierarchy, which level of needs forms the base of the pyramid?

options.A: Self-actualization
options.B: Safety and security
options.C: Love and belonging
options.D: Physiological needs

explanation: Physiological needs like air, water, and food sit at the very bottom of the pyramid because they are essential for immediate survival. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: A patient experiencing severe shortness of breath is unlikely to focus on which type of need at that moment?

options.A: Getting enough oxygen into the lungs
options.B: Achieving personal growth and self-actualization
options.C: Maintaining basic fluid balance
options.D: Relieving physical pain

explanation: Until basic physiological survival needs like breathing are met, higher-level needs such as self-actualization take a back seat. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is considered a primary physiological need?

options.A: Oxygen
options.B: Financial security
options.C: Friendship
options.D: Personal achievement

explanation: Oxygen is a critical physiological need required immediately to sustain life and cellular function. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: A patient recovering from abdominal surgery has not passed gas or had a bowel movement in three days. Which basic need is primarily affected?

options.A: Elimination
options.B: Safety and security
options.C: Love and belonging
options.D: Self-esteem

explanation: Bowel function falls under physiological elimination needs, which nurses closely monitor post-operatively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: Keeping a hospital patient's call bell within easy reach is an action primarily aimed at meeting which type of need?

options.A: Love and belonging
options.B: Physiological rest
options.C: Self-actualization
options.D: Safety and security

explanation: A call bell gives the patient a way to call for help, satisfying their need for physical and environmental safety. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: How do nurses help fulfill a hospitalized patient's need for emotional safety?

options.A: By limiting visits from family members completely
options.B: By performing procedures quickly without warning
options.C: By keeping information about treatments a secret
options.D: By explaining procedures clearly and answering questions honestly

explanation: Clear communication reduces anxiety and helps patients feel secure and in control of their situation. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which nursing action best supports a patient's need for love and belonging?

options.A: Focusing solely on medication schedules and vital signs
options.B: Encouraging family presence and active involvement in care
options.C: Minimizing conversation to prevent emotional attachment
options.D: Restricting all visitors to maintain hospital quiet hours

explanation: Involving family and loved ones helps maintain vital social connections that fulfill the need for belonging. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why can prolonged isolation during a hospital stay negatively impact physical recovery?

options.A: Loneliness and lack of social support can worsen stress and delay healing
options.B: Patients without visitors automatically stop taking prescribed drugs
options.C: Social isolation directly causes elevated blood glucose levels
options.D: Isolation increases the body's need for intravenous fluids

explanation: Psychosocial distress triggers physiological stress responses that can weaken immunity and slow down recovery times. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to protect a patient's self-esteem during personal care activities?

options.A: Promote independence and maintain patient privacy
options.B: Expose the entire body to finish the task faster
options.C: Perform all tasks without letting the patient help
options.D: Ignore the patient's preferences regarding privacy

explanation: Protecting privacy and encouraging patients to do what they can for themselves preserves their dignity and self-esteem. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of supporting self-esteem and self-actualization in patient care?

options.A: Listening respectfully when a patient expresses fears about the future
options.B: Dismissing a patient's personal spiritual beliefs as unimportant
options.C: Allowing a patient to make choices about their daily schedule
options.D: Celebrating small recovery milestones with the patient

explanation: Dismissing personal beliefs undermines respect and dignity, whereas supporting choices and listening builds self-worth. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h6)

question: How does cultural background typically influence a patient's basic human needs?

options.A: It shapes dietary practices, modesty, and views on health
options.B: Culture has no impact on health preferences
options.C: It dictates the exact vital sign ranges for all people
options.D: Culture only affects psychological self-actualization

explanation: Culture strongly guides how individuals view health, express pain, and practice dietary or personal habits. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why must a nurse consider a patient's developmental stage when assessing basic needs?

options.A: Developmental stages only matter in pediatric psychiatric units
options.B: All patients require the exact same nursing interventions regardless of age
options.C: An infant's physiological and safety needs differ significantly from an adult's
options.D: Older adults no longer have physiological needs

explanation: Age dictates specific physical vulnerabilities and capabilities, changing how nurses approach basic care requirements. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h7)

question: During which phase of the nursing process does the nurse actually perform interventions like wound care or medication administration?

options.A: Implementation
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Evaluation
options.D: Planning

explanation: Implementation is the action phase where the nurse carries out the planned care interventions. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: A nurse checks a patient's blood pressure thirty minutes after giving a blood pressure medication to see if it dropped into the normal range. Which phase of the nursing process is this?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Assessment

explanation: Checking the results after an intervention to see if goals were met is the definition of the evaluation phase. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of a professional nursing organization?

options.A: To protect, advance, and unify the nursing profession
options.B: To provide free medical insurance to members
options.C: To replace state nursing licensing boards
options.D: To handle hospital payroll disputes for all staff

explanation: These organizations exist primarily to uplift the nursing profession as a whole, set standards, and give nurses a collective voice. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why are professional nursing organizations important for your everyday life as a nurse?

options.A: They supply all consumable medical equipment to hospitals
options.B: They establish practice standards and shape health policies
options.C: They dictate the exact daily schedule of ward nurses
options.D: They manage direct disciplinary action for individual negligence

explanation: Think of these organizations as the voice of the profession. By creating guidelines and advocating for better policies, they help ensure safe, high-quality patient care everywhere.

question: What is a major personal benefit of joining a professional nursing body as a student or young nurse?

options.A: Automatic pay raises negotiated by the national body
options.B: Guaranteed promotion to head nurse within a year
options.C: Opportunities for networking and career growth
options.D: Exemption from paying annual state license renewal fees

explanation: Joining lets you connect with senior nurses and mentors who can help guide your career path and open doors to exciting opportunities!

question: You want to learn the latest wound care practices for your clinicals. How can a professional organization help you with this?

options.A: Direct supervision of the nurse during clinical dressing changes
options.B: Access to peer-reviewed professional journals and research
options.C: Immediate financial grants for personal housing and transport
options.D: Free medical supplies delivered directly to the hospital ward

explanation: Professional bodies regularly publish journals filled with fresh, evidence-based research so you can easily keep your clinical skills up to date.

question: What is the main focus of a national nursing organization like NANNM?

options.A: Country-specific labor laws and domestic health policies
options.B: Directing medical research for pharmaceutical corporations
options.C: Global monetary funds for hospital construction worldwide
options.D: Setting international travel guidelines for nurse migration

explanation: National bodies focus right at home—handling local working conditions, salaries, and health policies that directly affect nurses in our country.

question: How does a global body like the International Council of Nurses (ICN) differ from a local national association?

options.A: The ICN writes the specific nursing school curricula for every country
options.B: The ICN manages local salary disputes for individual clinics
options.C: The ICN directly licenses nurses to work in specific hospitals
options.D: The ICN federates national associations to address global health issues

explanation: While national bodies look at local laws, the ICN brings different countries together to tackle worldwide challenges like nursing shortages and global health policies.

question: Why is it better for nurses to advocate together through an organization rather than fighting alone at the bedside?

options.A: It removes the legal duty of care from individual practitioners
options.B: It prevents hospital management from ever questioning a nurse
options.C: It guarantees that all patient complaints are immediately dismissed
options.D: It gives nurses a stronger political voice to influence health laws

explanation: Politicians and policy-makers listen much more closely to an organized group representing thousands of healthcare workers than to a single voice!

question: Which of these is NOT a job of a professional nursing organization when it comes to ethics?

options.A: Promoting values like patient autonomy and justice
options.B: Drafting and updating the code of ethics for the profession
options.C: Issuing personal loans to nurses in financial distress
options.D: Guiding members on how to handle moral dilemmas

explanation: Professional bodies write our ethical codes and help us navigate tough clinical choices, but they don't operate as financial banks or loan providers.

question: What does CEU stand for in the context of professional nursing development?

options.A: Clinical Evaluation Uniform
options.B: Continuing Education Unit
options.C: Core Emergency Utilization
options.D: Certified Expert Underwriter

explanation: CEUs measure the hours of continuing education a nurse completes to maintain active competence and license renewal. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h5)

question: To renew your nursing license later on, you need proof of ongoing learning. How do professional organizations usually help you get this?

options.A: By providing free textbooks for basic nursing school entrance exams
options.B: By granting automatic license renewals without any coursework
options.C: By offering structured workshops and continuing education courses
options.D: By paying the state licensing board fees directly for the nurse

explanation: Professional organizations provide approved educational programs and workshops that give you the exact learning credits you need for license renewal.

question: What is the main goal of public health agencies, as opposed to a regular hospital ward?

options.A: Managing health at a population level
options.B: Training medical doctors exclusively
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Providing surgical operations only

explanation: You've got this! While hospital wards focus on one sick patient at a time, public health agencies look at the big picture—keeping whole communities healthy and preventing disease.

question: Why is it important for a clinical nurse to know about health maintenance agencies?

options.A: Agency guidelines dictate daily hospital protocols and safety standards
options.B: Nurses must directly fund these large government organizations
options.C: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on individual patient tips
options.D: Clinical nurses are legally required to manage agency budgets

explanation: Spot on! The rules, safety protocols, and daily routines we follow in the wards come directly from these health agencies.

question: Which Nigerian agency leads the charge when there is a disease outbreak or epidemic?

options.A: West African Examination Council
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works
options.C: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control
options.D: National Union of Road Transport

explanation: Great job! The NCDC is our frontline hero in Nigeria for spotting, stopping, and managing infectious disease outbreaks nationwide.

question: A community nurse needs official guidelines to start a new polio vaccine drive. Where is the best place to check first?

options.A: International fashion magazines
options.B: Private pharmaceutical marketing flyers
options.C: Local hospital cafeteria menus
options.D: National public health agency directives

explanation: Exactly! National health agencies provide the official schedules and steps that community health workers rely on for immunization campaigns.

question: What is the main job of international health organizations like the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: Setting local hospital staffing wages across individual states
options.B: Punishing nurses who fail bedside board examinations
options.C: Directing international health and managing global health security
options.D: Running private clinics in major capital cities

explanation: You got it! The WHO helps coordinate responses to global health crises and sets international standards that keep the whole world safer.

question: Why do infectious disease outbreaks often require international teamwork?

options.A: Infectious diseases easily cross national borders and spread globally
options.B: International agencies hold the patent on all known antibiotics
options.C: Local hospitals refuse to treat contagious patients
options.D: National governments lack any interest in stopping local outbreaks

explanation: Viruses and bacteria don't check passports at the border! Because germs spread fast across countries, countries must work together to stop pandemics.

question: What is a major task for an epidemiological nurse working in a public health agency?

options.A: Managing hospital financial investments
options.B: Cleaning and sterilizing surgical theater floors
options.C: Collecting data and tracking disease occurrences
options.D: Performing complex open-heart surgeries

explanation: Spot on! Epidemiological nurses are like health detectives—they track how diseases spread, gather infection numbers, and report outbreaks.

question: How does a public health nurse's daily role differ from a nurse working on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Agency nurses never interact with actual human patients
options.B: Agency nurses focus on community-wide prevention rather than individual bedside treatment
options.C: Hospital nurses write all national healthcare laws
options.D: Agency nurses only dispense emergency medications

explanation: Well done! Ward nurses care for patients one-on-one at the bedside, while public health nurses look at whole communities and prevention strategies.

question: Why do we have a structured referral system between primary clinics and large teaching hospitals?

options.A: Preventing tertiary hospitals from ever seeing complex cases
options.B: Ensuring patients receive the appropriate level of care efficiently
options.C: Increasing the financial cost of routine patient visits
options.D: Keeping patients in primary clinics for as long as possible

explanation: Exactly! The referral system makes sure patients get sent to the right facility that has the exact equipment and specialists they need.

question: A clinic patient has a severe heart condition that your primary health center cannot manage. What should you do next?

options.A: Discharging the patient with instructions to rest at home
options.B: Telling the patient that no further medical help exists
options.C: Attempting advanced cardiac surgery directly at the primary clinic
options.D: Initiating a formal referral to a tertiary cardiac center

explanation: You nailed it! When a patient's needs are beyond your clinic's scope, safely referring them upward to a tertiary center is the best nursing action.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge faced by public health agencies in developing regions?

options.A: Poor infrastructure delaying medical supply distribution
options.B: Shortages of trained public health professionals
options.C: Excessive, unlimited financial funding and surplus resources
options.D: Insufficient funding and budget constraints

explanation: Correct! Health agencies sadly almost never have a surplus of cash; they usually struggle with underfunding and resource shortages.

question: How do digital technologies help modern health maintenance agencies do their jobs better?

options.A: They prevent all infectious diseases from ever occurring again
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for any human nurses
options.C: They replace the need for clean water and sanitation programs
options.D: They enable real-time electronic disease surveillance and faster responses

explanation: Spot on! Digital tools and electronic tracking help agencies spot outbreaks instantly, replacing slow paper files with lightning-fast updates.

question: What is the key trait of a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on surgical nursing care
options.B: Training across multiple clinical specialties
options.C: Specializing in pediatric medicine only
options.D: Working only in hospital management roles

explanation: Spot on! A polyvalent nurse is cross-trained in different fields, meaning they can comfortably move and work across various hospital departments.

question: Why are polyvalent nurses a lifesaver during staff shortages?

options.A: They only work during night shifts
options.B: They do not require supervision from senior staff
options.C: They can be deployed easily to different hospital units
options.D: They demand lower salaries than specialized nurses

explanation: You got it! Because they have a mix of skills, hospitals can easily move them to busy or understaffed wards to keep patient care running smoothly.

question: In polyvalent nursing, what does giving 'holistic care' mean?

options.A: Focusing strictly on medication administration schedules
options.B: Prioritizing hospital administrative rules over patients
options.C: Treating only the specific disease diagnosed by a doctor
options.D: Looking at the whole person including body and mind

explanation: Exactly! Holistic care means looking at the patient as a complete human being—body, mind, and spirit—rather than just focusing on a single symptom.

question: What keeps a polyvalent nurse eager to keep learning on the job?

options.A: The desire to become a hospital administrator eventually
options.B: The need to maintain skills across many different medical fields
options.C: Pressure from hospital managers to reduce operating costs
options.D: Strict government laws requiring annual license renewals

explanation: Well done! Since they work in diverse units, polyvalent nurses always stay on their toes, updating their knowledge across multiple specialties.

question: What does 'multi-skilling' mean for a nurse?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff rosters
options.B: Possessing certified competence in various clinical tasks
options.C: Being able to perform minor surgeries without a doctor
options.D: Knowing how to operate heavy hospital machinery only

explanation: Correct! Multi-skilling is all about mastering a variety of practical nursing procedures so you can handle different types of patient care.

question: A nurse smoothly moves from managing an IV drip in the ER to dressing a wound in the surgical ward. What is this nurse showing?

options.A: Avoidance of heavy patient workloads
options.B: Strict adherence to departmental silos
options.C: Inability to focus on one single duty
options.D: Multi-skilling and clinical versatility

explanation: Spot on! Being able to switch tasks across different units proves you have great clinical versatility and multi-skilling abilities.

question: Where can polyvalent nurses put their skills to work?

options.A: Solely in out-patient community pharmacies
options.B: Only within government-run research laboratories
options.C: Across various urban and rural health facilities
options.D: Exclusively in private intensive care units

explanation: You nailed it! Because they are so adaptable, polyvalent nurses can fit right into almost any healthcare setting, from city hospitals to village clinics.

question: Why is adaptability so important for nurses working in rural clinics?

options.A: They follow rigid routines that never change
options.B: They often face limited resources and must adjust quickly
options.C: They deal exclusively with surgical trauma cases daily
options.D: They do not need to interact with other health workers

explanation: Correct! Rural clinics often lack heavy equipment and specialized staff, so nurses have to be resourceful and flexible to help their patients.

question: How does a polyvalent nurse usually support the healthcare team?

options.A: Deciding the hospital budget for medical supplies
options.B: Writing hospital policies without consulting staff
options.C: Replacing doctors during surgical operations
options.D: Acting as a communication link between different specialists

explanation: Spot on! They bridge the gaps between various medical professionals, keeping communication flowing for the patient's benefit.

question: Why is teamwork and good communication so great for patients?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any nursing documentation
options.B: It lowers the cost of private hospital rooms
options.C: It reduces the total time doctors spend in the hospital
options.D: It prevents errors and ensures coordinated treatment

explanation: You got it! When everyone on the healthcare team communicates well, patient care becomes much safer and better organized.

question: When does a polyvalent nurse need critical thinking the most?

options.A: When ordering food supplies for the hospital canteen
options.B: When organizing the staff holiday duty roster
options.C: When filing daily paperwork at the nurses' station
options.D: When analyzing sudden changes in a patient's condition

explanation: Exactly! Critical thinking helps you spot trouble early, figure out what's happening when a patient suddenly takes a turn for the worse, and act fast.

question: What should a polyvalent nurse do if standard supplies run out during an emergency?

options.A: Abandon the patient until fresh supplies arrive
options.B: Use problem-solving skills to find safe alternatives
options.C: Wait for the hospital director to fix the issue
options.D: Blame the junior nursing staff for the shortage

explanation: Well done! Resourcefulness is key in nursing. Finding safe alternatives keeps patients protected even when supplies are low.

question: What should you do if asked to perform a task outside your training and scope of practice?

options.A: Decline the task based on your scope of practice
options.B: Perform it anyway to help out the busy department
options.C: Pretend you completed the task on the patient's chart
options.D: Ask a patient to teach you how to do it

explanation: Spot on! Always stay within your legal and certified scope of practice. Patient safety comes first, and it's okay to say no to things you aren't trained for yet.

question: Which of these actions goes AGAINST a nurse's ethical duties?

options.A: Sharing patient medical details on social media
options.B: Advocating for the best interests of the sick person
options.C: Protecting patient privacy and medical confidentiality
options.D: Respecting the cultural beliefs of every patient

explanation: Correct! Patient confidentiality is sacred. Sharing patient details online is a serious breach of ethics and professional trust.

question: What major staffing headache in Nigerian healthcare do polyvalent nurses help solve?

options.A: A lack of patients seeking medical treatment
options.B: Shortages of specialized nursing personnel in facilities
options.C: An oversupply of doctors in rural health centers
options.D: Excessive funding for primary health care clinics

explanation: You got it! They are a wonderful solution for bridging the gap where specialized nurses are hard to find.

question: A rural health clinic has only two nurses on duty. Which staffing approach ensures the best care for the community?

options.A: Firing the nurses and hiring administrative clerks
options.B: Employing polyvalent nurses trained in multiple care areas
options.C: Restricting care strictly to adult male patients
options.D: Closing the clinic until a specialist doctor arrives

explanation: Spot on! Having polyvalent nurses means a small team can safely and confidently handle a wide variety of health needs in the community.

question: Which level of the Nigerian healthcare system includes federal teaching hospitals and specialized medical centers?

options.A: Community healthcare level
options.B: Secondary healthcare level
options.C: Tertiary healthcare level
options.D: Primary healthcare level

explanation: Teaching hospitals and federal medical centers operate at the tertiary level to provide advanced and specialized care. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of primary healthcare centers in Nigeria?

options.A: Basic preventive services and community health
options.B: Complex neurosurgeries and organ transplants
options.C: Long-term rehabilitation for chronic stroke
options.D: Advanced medical research and drug trials

explanation: Primary health centers handle grassroots care, immunizations, and treatment of common minor conditions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h1)

question: Where is the nurses' station typically placed in a modern hospital ward?

options.A: At the center to allow clear sightlines
options.B: Near the entrance to restrict visitor access
options.C: At the far end away from patient beds
options.D: Inside the main doctor consulting room

explanation: Central placement helps staff monitor patient activity and respond quickly to call bells or emergencies. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why does a hospital ward have separate clean utility and dirty utility rooms?

options.A: To comply with fire safety evacuation rules
options.B: To give nurses a private space to take meal breaks
options.C: To separate male patients from female patients
options.D: To prevent cross-contamination between sterile supplies and waste

explanation: Separation ensures clean medical supplies do not mix with used equipment, body fluids, or waste items. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h2)

question: Who holds overall administrative and clinical responsibility for running a hospital ward?

options.A: The senior ward orderly
options.B: The Chief Medical Director
options.C: The hospital head pharmacist
options.D: The Ward Manager or Nursing Officer in Charge

explanation: The Ward Manager handles staff scheduling, clinical standards, and general administrative duties on the unit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h3)

question: A student nurse is assigned to give medications on the ward. What is the correct way to supervise this task?

options.A: Provide direct clinical supervision while medications are given
options.B: Allow senior patients to help the student verify doses
options.C: Delegate the supervision entirely to the ward cleaner
options.D: Let the student complete all drug rounds independently

explanation: Students must always be supervised by qualified staff to protect patient safety during clinical procedures. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of a nursing shift handover on the ward?

options.A: To give doctors time to complete patient medical notes
options.B: To distribute weekly salaries to the nursing staff
options.C: To allow the hospital management to inspect ward cleanliness
options.D: To pass critical patient updates between incoming and outgoing staff

explanation: Handover ensures continuous, safe care by briefing the incoming shift on each patient's current status and needs. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h4)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for in the ISBAR communication tool used during clinical handovers?

options.A: Symptoms and Surgery
options.B: Situation and Background
options.C: Salary and Station
options.D: Sterile and Safe

explanation: In ISBAR, S stands for Situation and Background, helping nurses structure clinical communication clearly. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which waste bin color is strictly designated for used sharps and needles in a Nigerian hospital ward?

options.A: Yellow bag
options.B: Green bucket
options.C: Black bin
options.D: Sharps box

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps boxes prevent needle stick injuries among healthcare workers and waste handlers. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h5)

question: A nurse finishes dressing a wound soaked with infected pus. Where should the soiled gauze dressing be discarded?

options.A: Cardboard medication box
options.B: General recycling container
options.C: Yellow infectious waste bag
options.D: Black domestic waste bin

explanation: Infectious clinical waste containing body fluids goes into the yellow bag to prevent the spread of pathogens. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h5)

question: How often should essential emergency equipment like crash carts be checked on a hospital ward?

options.A: Every shift
options.B: Once a month
options.C: Only after a patient codes
options.D: Once a year

explanation: Routine shift checks ensure that emergency items are present, functional, and ready for immediate use. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the correct immediate action when a nurse discovers a vital sign monitor has a broken power cord?

options.A: Continue using it with the broken wire taped up
options.B: Hide it inside the nurse's locker until the manager returns
options.C: Throw it directly into the black domestic waste bin
options.D: Label it out of service and report it for repair

explanation: Faulty electrical equipment poses severe hazards and must be removed from use and reported right away. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is an essential responsibility during a patient's admission to the ward?

options.A: Conducting a formal hospital billing audit
options.B: Prescribing complex specialist surgical medications
options.C: Discharging the patient immediately to free up the bed
options.D: Providing orientation to the ward and taking baseline vitals

explanation: Admitting a patient involves settling them in, measuring baseline vitals, and explaining ward routines. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why is proper health education important before a patient is discharged from the ward?

options.A: To ensure the patient understands home care and medication routines
options.B: To replace the need for follow-up clinic appointments
options.C: To convince the patient to stay longer in the hospital
options.D: To test the patient on their reading and writing skills

explanation: Discharge education helps prevent readmission by teaching patients how to care for themselves at home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h7)

question: How many main tiers make up Nigeria's public healthcare system?

options.A: Three distinct levels of care
options.B: Five distinct levels of care
options.C: Two distinct levels of care
options.D: Four distinct levels of care

explanation: Think of Nigeria's health setup like a ladder with three steps: primary, secondary, and tertiary. Each level is built to handle specific types of health needs in our communities!

question: Why do we use a tiered, step-by-step system for healthcare delivery in Nigeria?

options.A: To make sure every health problem is handled at a teaching hospital
options.B: To restrict patient movement completely between rural and urban areas
options.C: To properly match the severity of health problems with the right facility
options.D: To ensure care is given based on how wealthy a patient is

explanation: Organizing care into tiers keeps things practical! Simple issues get solved right in the neighborhood, while complex cases go to well-equipped specialist centers.

question: What is the main job of a primary health care facility?

options.A: To serve as the first point of contact for community health needs
options.B: To train resident doctors and medical specialists
options.C: To provide long-term care for chronic psychiatric disorders
options.D: To perform major surgical operations like brain surgery

explanation: Primary health centers are right there in the community. They are the friendly first stop for everyday health needs and prevention.

question: Which service would you most expect to find at a local primary health care center?

options.A: Sub-specialty pediatric neurology consultations
options.B: Advanced cancer chemotherapy and radiation therapy
options.C: Routine childhood immunization and antenatal care
options.D: Complex open-heart surgical procedures

explanation: Primary health centers focus heavily on community wellness. That means giving babies their routine vaccines and supporting mothers with antenatal care every day!

question: Which of these represents secondary healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: Private herbal research institutes
options.B: General and state specialist hospitals
options.C: Local village health posts
options.D: Federal university teaching hospitals

explanation: General hospitals and state specialist hospitals are our go-to secondary facilities, offering different specialty departments to care for admitted patients.

question: A patient has a complicated hernia that a local clinic cannot manage. Where should they be sent?

options.A: A community immunization desk
options.B: A traditional bone setter
options.C: A secondary health facility
options.D: A primary health post

explanation: Surgical procedures like hernia repairs that need admission to a hospital ward are managed at secondary health facilities like general hospitals.

question: What is a key feature that makes a tertiary health facility unique?

options.A: It only handles uncomplicated outpatient malaria cases
options.B: It is the first point of contact in a rural village
options.C: It provides basic immunization only
options.D: It serves as a center for training and medical research

explanation: Tertiary hospitals (like our teaching hospitals) do double duty: they provide advanced patient care while training future healthcare heroes and conducting medical research.

question: What is the main difference between tertiary and secondary healthcare?

options.A: Tertiary care involves highly specialized sub-specialists and advanced technology
options.B: Tertiary care is located in every small rural village across the country
options.C: Secondary care requires medical students for operation, unlike tertiary care
options.D: Secondary care handles complex brain surgery while tertiary care handles basic immunization

explanation: When cases get super complex, they go to tertiary centers. They have advanced technology and sub-specialists that standard general hospitals don't usually have.

question: What is the primary focus of social services in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Performing major orthopedic surgeries in the operating theatre
options.B: Addressing non-medical social and economic challenges affecting health
options.C: Conducting laboratory blood tests and urinalysis
options.D: Prescribing strong antibiotics for bacterial infections

explanation: Good health isn't just about medicine! Social services look at things like poverty, living conditions, and family support that affect how well a patient recovers.

question: A patient is medically ready to leave the ward, but has no home, money, or family support. Who is best suited to help?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist
options.B: The laboratory scientist
options.C: The medical social worker
options.D: The chief operating surgeon

explanation: Medical social workers are champions at discharge planning! They help find shelter and connect vulnerable patients with community support systems.

question: What is an inter-referral pathway in healthcare?

options.A: A list of pharmacy prices for essential drugs in the market
options.B: A route taken by ambulance drivers to avoid heavy traffic congestion
options.C: A schedule for nursing shift change handovers on the ward
options.D: A structured system for moving patients between different levels of care

explanation: An inter-referral pathway is just a smooth roadmap for transferring a patient from a smaller clinic up to a bigger hospital when they need more specialized help.

question: Why is clear paperwork and documentation so important when transferring a patient to a teaching hospital?

options.A: To prove to the hospital management that nurses are working hard
options.B: To increase the hospital billing charges for the patient
options.C: To ensure continuity of care and prevent treatment delays
options.D: To make the patient's folder look bulky and professional

explanation: Good transfer notes give the new team a clear history of what has been done, making sure the patient keeps getting safe, uninterrupted care without repeating tests.

question: How does a nurse's role in a primary health center usually differ from working in a big teaching hospital?

options.A: Primary nurses work with greater independence in community wellness and prevention
options.B: Tertiary nurses never administer medications or check vital signs
options.C: Primary nurses only perform complex open-heart surgeries daily
options.D: Tertiary nurses do not require any formal nursing education

explanation: At a primary health center, nurses often run clinics independently, focusing heavily on health promotion, immunizations, and spotting community health issues early.

question: Which of these is NOT a core duty expected of a nurse, no matter where they work?

options.A: Performing major neurosurgical operations independently
options.B: Administering prescribed medications safely
options.C: Advocating for the health and safety of patients
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and clinical progress

explanation: Surgeries like brain operations are strictly done by trained surgeons, not nurses, regardless of whether it's a primary clinic or a tertiary hospital!

question: Who do we traditionally call a 'patient' in a healthcare setting?

options.A: An active partner who solely directs their own medical treatment
options.B: An individual receiving medical treatment for a disease or injury
options.C: A person who only seeks wellness advice in a community hall
options.D: A healthcare professional working inside a tertiary hospital

explanation: You got this! A patient is simply someone who is dealing with an illness or injury and getting care from medical pros.

question: Why do we often use the word 'client' instead of 'patient' in community health nursing?

options.A: It indicates that the person is suffering from an acute terminal illness
options.B: It removes the need for any documentation by the nursing staff
options.C: It highlights cannabis use and lifestyle choices
options.D: It highlights the person as an active partner in their own health

explanation: Spot on! Calling someone a 'client' shows they play an active role in their health journey, rather than just being a passive receiver of care.

question: How is 'wellness' best understood in nursing?

options.A: The total elimination of chronic disease through surgical intervention
options.B: The complete absence of any physical or psychological discomfort
options.C: An active, lifelong process of making choices toward optimal well-being
options.D: A temporary state that only occurs when a person is admitted to a ward

explanation: Great job! Wellness isn't just about not being sick; it's a daily, lifelong journey of making healthy choices for your mind and body.

question: Can a person experience wellness even if they have a chronic illness?

options.A: No, chronic illnesses automatically prevent any form of social well-being
options.B: Yes, but only if they completely stop taking all prescribed medications
options.C: No, because wellness requires the total absence of any medical diagnosis
options.D: Yes, by effectively managing their condition and maintaining a positive outlook

explanation: Exactly! Having a chronic condition doesn't mean you can't live a full, happy life with proper self-care and a good mindset.

question: What is a very common feeling for someone newly admitted to a hospital?

options.A: Complete emotional indifference to surroundings
options.B: Anxiety and a sense of vulnerability
options.C: Total independence over institutional schedules
options.D: Overwhelming joy regarding hospital routines

explanation: True story! Hospitals can feel strange and intimidating, so it's normal for newly admitted patients to feel a bit anxious and exposed.

question: Why should nurses pay close attention to the worries of hospitalized patients?

options.A: It allows the nurse to shorten the visiting hours for relatives
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will pay their medical bills on time
options.C: Patients prefer strict institutional schedules over personal freedom
options.D: Fear and powerlessness can negatively impact healing and compliance

explanation: Well thought out! When patients are too stressed or scared, it can actually slow down their physical recovery and make them less likely to follow treatment.

question: Where do community health clients usually receive their care?

options.A: In their natural environments like homes, schools, and workplaces
options.B: Exclusively inside specialized intensive care hospital units
options.C: Inside locked psychiatric wards during involuntary confinement
options.D: Only within private surgical suites following major operations

explanation: You got it! Community nursing meets people right where they live, work, and go to school instead of keeping them in a hospital.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care out in the community?

options.A: Health education, disease prevention, and personal empowerment
options.B: Performing major surgical operations in local community halls
options.C: Managing acute life-threatening trauma without medical backup
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital visiting hours and meal schedules

explanation: Spot on! Community nurses focus on teaching people how to stay healthy and take charge of their own wellness.

question: Which of these is a key feature of institutional (hospital) care?

options.A: Complete client autonomy over daily schedules
options.B: Reliance solely on family members for medical tasks
options.C: A controlled and unfamiliar hospital setting
options.D: Delivery of services exclusively inside private homes

explanation: Correct! Institutional care happens in hospitals where routines and environments are strictly managed by the healthcare team.

question: How does community-based care differ from hospital care regarding patient freedom?

options.A: There is no difference in personal autonomy between the two settings
options.B: Institutional care gives patients more freedom to choose their meal times
options.C: Community care relies strictly on hospital staff to dictate daily actions
options.D: Community care allows clients greater autonomy over their daily routines

explanation: Brilliant! At home, clients keep their freedom and call the shots on their everyday daily routines.

question: What is a major duty of a nurse working in a hospital ward?

options.A: Living with families to supervise their daily meal preparation
options.B: Building local community infrastructure and public roads
options.C: Acting as a direct caregiver and monitor of acute treatments
options.D: Operating primary health clinics without physician oversight

explanation: Right on! Hospital nurses spend their shifts giving hands-on care, giving meds, and keeping a close eye on acutely ill patients.

question: How does a community health nurse's role differ from a hospital nurse?

options.A: The community nurse has no responsibility for patient health outcomes
options.B: The community nurse spends all shift managing mechanical ventilators
options.C: The community nurse strictly follows rigid hospital visiting rules
options.D: The community nurse focuses more on education, advocacy, and resource linkage

explanation: You nailed it! Community nurses shine by teaching populations and connecting families to health resources around them.

question: What is a major reason people in Nigeria often delay going to modern hospitals?

options.A: An excess of free hospitals in every rural village
options.B: Mandatory international health insurance for all citizens
options.C: The complete absence of any traditional healing practices
options.D: Financial constraints and out-of-pocket health spending

explanation: True. Having to pay out-of-pocket without easy health insurance often makes folks wait until an illness gets really bad before seeking care.

question: Why must Nigerian nurses understand local health-seeking behaviors?

options.A: To eliminate the need for community health outreach programs
options.B: To prove that traditional medicine has no value in society
options.C: To provide culturally sensitive care and bridge traditional and modern practices
options.D: To force every patient to completely abandon their religious beliefs

explanation: Spot on! When we respect cultural beliefs and money realities, we can build trust and safely guide patients to the best medical care.

question: What does giving 'holistic nursing care' mean?

options.A: Exclusively treating the biological cause of the acute disease
options.B: The physical, emotional, social, and spiritual dimensions of the client
options.C: Strictly checking the financial cost of prescribed drugs
options.D: Only looking at physical lab test results on the chart

explanation: Fantastic! Holistic care means treating the whole person—body, mind, emotions, and spirit, not just a disease.

question: What is the biggest benefit of practicing patient-centred care?

options.A: It ensures that hospital administration saves money on supplies
options.B: It allows the nurse to ignore the patient's personal opinions
options.C: It builds trust and significantly enhances overall health outcomes
options.D: It removes the requirement for nursing documentation

explanation: You got it! When patients feel respected and involved in their care, they trust us more and heal much better.

question: What does viewing a patient in their social context primarily involve?

options.A: Isolating the patient from family members during treatment
options.B: Recognizing how relationships and living conditions affect health
options.C: Focusing strictly on the diseased organ and laboratory values
options.D: Prioritizing hospital policies over community traditions

explanation: Social context looks at the broader picture of a person's life, including family and living conditions, which deeply influence health outcomes. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why might a clinically successful hospital treatment fail once the patient goes home?

options.A: Hospital laboratories are always more accurate than home testing
options.B: The patient's home environment and social support were ignored
options.C: Doctors usually prescribe the wrong medications for home use
options.D: Nurses fail to document the discharge date properly

explanation: If a care plan does not fit a patient's real-life social and financial situation at home, they will struggle to follow it. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: According to family systems theory, what happens when one family member falls seriously ill?

options.A: Daily household routines remain entirely unchanged
options.B: Family income automatically increases to cover treatment
options.C: The balance of the entire household is disrupted
options.D: The other members become completely immune to the disease

explanation: Because family members are closely linked, an illness in one person creates a ripple effect that impacts everyone in the home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: A father is admitted for chronic hypertension. Why should the nurse involve his spouse and children in his discharge education?

options.A: Family members must take over the patient's job responsibilities
options.B: Hospital regulations require at least three visitors per patient
options.C: It prevents the patient from speaking to the doctor alone
options.D: The family functions as a unit, and lifestyle changes require household support

explanation: Diet and lifestyle changes are much easier to maintain when the whole family understands and participates in them. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which family structure typically has a wide pool of available caregivers living close by?

options.A: Extended family
options.B: Single-parent family
options.C: Nuclear family
options.D: Isolated family

explanation: Extended families include grandparents and other relatives who can easily share caregiving duties and emotional support. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a common health vulnerability frequently faced by single-parent households?

options.A: High financial strain and limited time for healthcare appointments
options.B: Too many conflicting medical opinions from relatives
options.C: Total immunity to common childhood infectious diseases
options.D: Excessive living space leading to social isolation

explanation: Single parents often carry the entire financial and domestic burden alone, making it hard to prioritize routine health visits. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a common result when a primary breadwinner develops a disabling chronic illness?

options.A: Automatic government provision of permanent housing
options.B: The complete elimination of domestic chores
options.C: Shifts in household roles and financial responsibilities
options.D: Immediate improvement in overall family communication

explanation: A major illness forces other family members to take over tasks previously managed by the sick individual. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: An adolescent daughter tells the nurse she is exhausted from missing school to look after her sick mother. What should the nurse recognize?

options.A: The family is experiencing role strain and needs additional support
options.B: The teenager is simply misbehaving and needs stricter discipline
options.C: The mother's illness has cured itself through natural rest
options.D: Normal adolescent development includes full-time caregiving

explanation: When children take on heavy caregiving roles, it signals that the family system is strained and requires outside intervention. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following is a primary way the community environment influences health?

options.A: Replacing the need for individual personal hygiene
options.B: Providing access to safe water, markets, and local clinics
options.C: Ensuring every citizen has a high-paying professional job
options.D: Eliminating all infectious diseases from the environment

explanation: Basic community infrastructure like clean water and nearby health clinics directly dictates physical well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: How can community cultural norms impact how people seek medical care?

options.A: They force doctors to change scientific medical facts
options.B: They can either encourage early treatment or promote harmful myths
options.C: They automatically guarantee high hospital attendance rates
options.D: They have zero effect on modern medical treatment choices

explanation: Beliefs shared within a community strongly influence whether people trust modern healthcare or rely solely on unproven remedies. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of using a genogram during a family nursing assessment?

options.A: To calculate the exact monthly income of the household
options.B: To track the daily caloric intake of the patient
options.C: To list all community parks near the patient's home
options.D: To map out inherited medical conditions across generations

explanation: A genogram acts as a detailed family tree that helps nurses identify hereditary health risks and family patterns. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is it important to include the family when creating a patient's care plan?

options.A: It legally forces the family to pay all hospital bills
options.B: It ensures the plan fits their routine and improves cooperation
options.C: It stops the doctor from making any changes to the treatment
options.D: It reduces the total number of nursing shifts required

explanation: When families help build the plan, they understand it better and are much more likely to help carry it out at home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is a primary role of a public health nurse in the community?

options.A: Connecting families to local health and social support resources
options.B: Writing national health policies for pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Managing the financial budgets of local government hospitals
options.D: Performing complex major surgeries in community centers

explanation: Public health nurses link individuals and families to clinics, support groups, and welfare services that promote wellbeing. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h7)

question: A discharged mother struggles to afford nutritious food for her infant. Which action by the nurse best shows community-focused care?

options.A: Advising her to stop feeding the infant until she finds a better job
options.B: Referring the mother to a local community food program or welfare service
options.C: Keeping the infant admitted in the acute hospital ward indefinitely
options.D: Telling her to buy more expensive imported baby formula immediately

explanation: Connecting the family to local community assistance helps solve the root social cause of their nutritional challenge. You're being a true advocate!

question: What is the primary goal of orienting a newly admitted patient to the ward?

options.A: To give the doctor time to finish other ward rounds
options.B: To test the patient's memory and cognitive function
options.C: To reduce anxiety and help them adjust to the new environment
options.D: To ensure the patient fills out their discharge papers early

explanation: A good orientation helps a frightened or stressed patient feel secure by showing them how things work around the ward. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why must a nurse demonstrate the call bell system immediately upon a patient's arrival?

options.A: It distracts the patient from their current physical pain
options.B: It gives the patient a direct way to call for help when needed
options.C: It proves to the visiting family members that the equipment works
options.D: Hospital policy requires it to be tested every single hour

explanation: Showing the patient the call bell ensures they can easily summon assistance for urgent needs like using the toilet or managing sudden pain. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: An admission that is planned well in advance for a scheduled surgical procedure is called what?

options.A: An elective admission
options.B: An emergency admission
options.C: A transfer admission
options.D: An acute admission

explanation: Elective admissions are scheduled ahead of time because the patient's condition is stable enough to wait for a convenient date. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the ward with a large amount of cash and expensive jewelry. What should the nurse do first regarding these valuables?

options.A: Tell the patient to wear the jewelry so nobody can steal it
options.B: Lock the cash inside the bedside table drawer and keep the key
options.C: Place the items in the open utility room for safe keeping
options.D: Follow hospital policy to document and secure the items safely

explanation: Valuables must be documented on an inventory list and stored securely according to hospital protocol, preferably sent home with family or locked in the main safe. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which piece of information is most critical to document immediately during a patient's admission assessment?

options.A: Known drug allergies
options.B: Favorite television programs
options.C: Previous occupation history
options.D: Preferred clothing brand

explanation: Documenting allergies immediately prevents the accidental administration of medications that could cause severe or life-threatening reactions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is it important to complete admission documentation promptly rather than waiting until the end of a long shift?

options.A: So that nurses can leave work before their shift officially ends
options.B: To allow the patient to take the paper home immediately
options.C: Because ward managers check handwriting speeds daily
options.D: To prevent forgetting important clinical details and ensure safety

explanation: Writing down observations immediately ensures accuracy and provides oncoming staff with up-to-date information for safe care delivery. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)
